source.reason: This block describes the heating/soaking stage applied to the sample and die prior to warm MAF at 250 °C, the thermal step of the MAF-5 process.

method.value: heating and soaking of sample and die

processing_steps_notes.value: Before MAF the sample and die are heated to 250 °C and soaked for two hours. 250 °C (warm deformation) is chosen because the alloy has the highest malleability between 150 °C and 450 °C, below the recrystallization temperature; temperatures above 450 °C would cause carbide precipitation.

source.reason: These blocks give the warm MAF parameters for the 5-pass sample: three orthogonal directions per pass, 250 °C, 33% normal strain per pass, ram speed 1 mm/s, MoS2 lubricant, 100 ton press, cumulative strain 2.3 and MAF-5 naming.

processing_steps_notes.value: 5 passes of MAF performed by compressing the billet in three mutually perpendicular directions (one pass = three orthogonal compressions) on a 100 ton hydraulic press, along three orthogonal directions. Initial billet 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm; height reduced from 30 mm to 20 mm each pass giving 33% normal strain per pass (equivalent strain per pass 0.47); cumulative equivalent strain ≈ 2.3. Ram moved at a steady speed of 1 mm/s; samples lubricated with MoS2 before pressing. The sample could only be forged five times before breaking on the sixth attempt; this final state is denoted MAF-5.

source.reason: The MAF-5 microstructure (single-phase austenitic with κ carbide reflections, refined lamellar grains, randomized texture, banded/blocky substructure) is described in the XRD and EBSD discussion blocks and the corresponding EBSD figures.

overall_structure.value: Austenite-based Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel. XRD shows the examined steels have only the majority austenite phase; after 5 MAF passes (MAF-5) the microstructure is heavily deformed with a banded/blocky substructure dominated by high-angle grain boundaries, a randomized (weakened) texture, refined lamellar grains and the highest dislocation density of the studied series.

region.value: Analysed area for XRD/EBSD (central shaded plate of the MAFed billet, mid-plane, normal/pressing direction)

morphology.value: lamellar grains (transverse dimension ~13 μm); banded/blocky substructure

texture.value: Texture randomised relative to the strongly textured solution-treated MAF-0; with increasing passes many more directions become parallel to the pressing direction and the grains become randomized.

source.reason: Text states that at 5 passes / total strain 2.3 the austenite grain size is further reduced ultimately reaching approximately 13 μm, and the Fig. 8 grain-size-vs-strain plot labels MAF-5 at 13 μm.

grain_size_distribution.value: The initial grain size distribution was relatively wide; as deformation progressed the distribution became narrower and more uniform for the 5th pass. MAF-5 shows the narrowest and lowest area-fraction distribution (peaking near 0.09 around 10-20 μm). In regions of high strain concentration there are variations in grain size.

texture.value: Randomized/weakened relative to MAF-0; the sample becomes less strongly textured and grains are randomized as the number of passes increases.

source.reason: These blocks report the grain-boundary character evolution (high/low angle fractions), the transformation of low- to high-angle boundaries after 5 passes, the absence of deformation twinning and the constant carbide state for MAF-5.

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: After 5 passes of MAF some low-angle boundaries convert to high-angle boundaries, raising the high-angle boundary fraction to 0.69 (0.699) while the low-angle boundary fraction falls to 0.301, producing a red-dominated banded/blocky substructure with the highest local misorientation (KAM 1.07°).
Dislocation density increases continuously to 8.98 × 10^15 m^-2 at 5 passes; at the critical strain 2.3 (five passes) the degree of increment decreases and dislocations rearrange.

phase_evolution.value: No deformation twinning occurs in this steel; a negligible annealing twin boundary fraction of 0.003 remains in MAF-5. Carbide (κ) reflections are unchanged before and after MAF, so precipitation strengthening is considered constant.

interface_notes.value: Grain boundaries located with misorientation > 15° are treated as grain boundaries (equivalent grain size method). High-angle (15°–180°) and low-angle (1°–15°) boundary fractions are used to track the microstructural evolution with MAF passes.

measurement_conditions.value: scan speed 2° per minute, step size 0.02°, 2θ range 40°–120°; electro-polished samples; instrumental peak broadening from standard silicon data subtracted

purpose.value: Estimate dislocation density from peak broadening (Williamson-Hall plot, Eq. 1), determine average lattice microstrain and crystallite size

key_findings.value: MAF-5: average crystallite size 10.12 nm, average microstrain 6.88 × 10^-3, dislocation density 8.98 × 10^15 m^-2; peaks broaden further relative to lower passes; γ(220) near 87° 2θ is the most intense reflection; majority austenite phase with κ carbide reflections retained; Burgers vector b = 0.259 nm

source.reason: These blocks describe the 3-D FE model of the MAF process, the ABAQUS/Explicit VUMAT implementation of the modified J-C model, boundary conditions/mesh, validation against experimental dislocation density, grain size and yield strength, and the constitutive/strengthening equations with their fitted parameters.

simulation_method.value: 3-D finite element simulation of the forging operation using explicit dynamics, with a modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model implemented through a VUMAT user-material subroutine

potential_model_or_database.value: Modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (Eq. 6) incorporating dislocation-density and grain-size strengthening; VUMAT subroutine with six state-dependent variables (SDV1 equivalent plastic strain, SDV2 equivalent plastic strain rate, SDV3 dislocation density ρf, SDV4 flow stress, SDV5 yield strength, SDV6 grain size df). Original J-C parameters from previous study [26].

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Workpiece 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm treated as a deformable body; die and punch treated as discrete rigid bodies; punch undergoes controlled displacement of 10 mm in Y (height) direction while die is fixed; layout permits material flow only in X (flow direction) and constrains flow in Z (constrained direction); overall contact friction coefficient 0.15; mesh sensitivity analysis gives optimal mesh size 0.6 mm; total 41382 hex elements (C3D8R) with reduced integration and hourglass control; steady-state MAF simulated by mapping previous-pass deformation fields to the current pass.

validation_against_experiment.value: The modified J-C model with FEA shows good agreement with measured dislocation density and grain size during MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5, and predicts good yield-strength values after each pass. Up to 3 passes the simulation predicts strengthening similar to the experimental values; after 3 passes the predicted value shows a lower deviation (the FE simulation underestimates the measured yield strength most strongly at 5 passes, attributed to texture effects not included in the simulation).

equation_role.value: flow stress: σ_flow = (σ0 + k(df^-1/2 − d0^-1/2) + αMGb(ρf^1/2 − ρ0^1/2) + Bε^n)[1 + C ln(ε̇/ε̇0)][1 − ((T−Tr)/(Tm−Tr))^m]

model_note.value: Adds grain-boundary strengthening (Hall-Petch) and dislocation (Taylor) strengthening terms to the standard J-C model so flow stress after each MAF pass is captured.
Empirical relation proposed by Singh et al. [41], fitted to the measured dislocation density vs imposed equivalent strain (Table 1, Fig. 6).
Exponential grain-refinement relation fitted to imposed equivalent strain vs grain size (Fig. 8(b)); k3 is a strengthening constant.
Contribution of refined grains (50–13 μm) to yield strength.
Contribution of dislocation density to yield strength.
At MAF-0 all strengthening parameters are included in σ0; solid-solution and precipitate strengthening are treated as constant across passes.

unmapped_findings: Average crystallite size of MAF-5 measured by XRD is 10.12 nm (Table 1, Fig. 6).

The yield-strength increase of MAF-5 over solution-annealed MAF-0 decomposes into 762 MPa attributable to the dislocation-density difference and 386 MPa attributable to grain refinement (Table 2, Fig. 8 region b0083).

Cumulative equivalent strain after 5 passes is 2.3 (33% normal strain per pass; equivalent strain per pass 0.47); the FE simulation gives a maximum central-region strain of approximately 2.6 after five passes, exceeding the applied external strain value of 2.3.
No deformation twinning occurs in this steel; a negligible annealing twin boundary fraction of 0.003 remains in MAF-5 (vs 0.007 in MAF-1).
The alloy could only be multiaxially forged a total of five times before breaking on the sixth attempt, so MAF-5 is the maximum-equivalent-strain state (2.3) studied at 250 °C.
